evals.name: bucket-a-python-signup
evals.prompt: I'm building a Python FastAPI service and I want to start monitoring it with MultiTool. I've never heard of MultiTool before today and don't have an account yet. The repo has a `requirements.txt` (with `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `pydantic` — no OpenTelemetry packages), a `main.py` with a basic FastAPI app, and a `Dockerfile`. We deploy to Fly.io and the Fly config exports `FLY_MACHINE_VERSION` (which Fly bumps every release) and `FLY_APP_NAME`. There's no .env file yet, but the project is in a git repo with a .gitignore. Walk me through what you'd do to get this set up end to end.
evals.expected_output: Should detect Python/FastAPI, identify Bucket A (no OTel installed), recommend opentelemetry-distro auto-instrumentation, walk through MultiTool signup via the bundled script (--signup mode), set up the Resource with all three mandatory attributes, and ideally suggest using FLY_MACHINE_VERSION as the service.version source rather than defaulting to APP_VERSION. Should add .env to .gitignore. Should use the X-API-KEY header. Should not actually invoke the script or AskUserQuestion — describe what you'd do instead.

evals.name: bucket-b-go-alongside
evals.prompt: We're a Go shop and we already send OTel traces to Honeycomb from our user-service. I want to evaluate MultiTool in parallel without losing Honeycomb data — both backends should receive every span during the evaluation. The OTel setup is in `internal/telemetry/tracing.go` — it builds an `otlptracehttp.New` exporter pointing at `api.honeycomb.io` with an `x-honeycomb-team` header, and a `trace.NewTracerProvider` with that exporter and a Resource that sets `service.name="user-service"`. The service runs in Kubernetes; we tag Docker images with the git SHA and the deployment yaml exports `GIT_SHA` and `ENVIRONMENT` env vars to the pod. I already have a MultiTool account but no API key for this service yet. How would you wire MultiTool in alongside Honeycomb?
evals.expected_output: Should detect Go, identify Bucket B, add MultiTool as a SECOND BatchSpanProcessor / WithBatcher on the same TracerProvider (NOT replace Honeycomb). Should use the existing GIT_SHA and ENVIRONMENT env vars for service.version and deployment.environment.name rather than introducing APP_VERSION / APP_ENVIRONMENT. Should walk through running the script in --login mode. Should add service.version and deployment.environment.name to the existing Resource (which currently only has service.name). Should use X-API-KEY header. Should not invoke the script or AskUserQuestion directly.

evals.name: bucket-d-typescript-legacy
evals.prompt:
I followed an older version of this MultiTool guide a few months ago to set up tracing for my TypeScript Express app. Traces ARE arriving in MultiTool, but my deploy timeline in the UI shows everything bucketed as "v1.0.0" — all my versions are collapsed. My `tracing.ts` looks like this:

```ts
import { NodeSDK } from '@opentelemetry/sdk-node'
import { OTLPTraceExporter } from '@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http'
import { Resource } from '@opentelemetry/resources'
import { SemanticResourceAttributes } from '@opentelemetry/semantic-conventions'
import { getNodeAutoInstrumentations } from '@opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node'

const sdk = new NodeSDK({
  resource: new Resource({
    [SemanticResourceAttributes.SERVICE_NAME]: 'my-api',
    [SemanticResourceAttributes.SERVICE_VERSION]: '1.0.0',
  }),
  traceExporter: new OTLPTraceExporter({
    url: 'https://api.multitool.run/otlp/v1/traces',
    headers: { 'api-key': process.env.MULTI_API_KEY ?? '' },
  }),
  instrumentations: [getNodeAutoInstrumentations()],
})
sdk.start()
```

I already have my MULTI_API_KEY set in the deployed env. CI exports `BUILD_SHA` to the runtime. Don't ask me to paste my key — just look at the code. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Should detect TypeScript, identify Bucket D (partial). Should identify THREE distinct problems: (1) service.version is hardcoded to '1.0.0' instead of read from a runtime source — should switch to process.env.BUILD_SHA since user mentioned CI exports that, (2) deployment.environment.name is missing entirely from the Resource, (3) the auth header is 'api-key' (lowercase) instead of 'X-API-KEY' — legacy from older skill. Should NOT ask about MultiTool account state (user has key). Should NOT rewrite or restructure code beyond fixing those three things. Should NOT ask the user to paste the key value.

evals.name: bucket-c-java-verify
evals.expected_output: Should detect Java/Spring Boot, identify Bucket C (fully correct). Endpoint is right, X-API-KEY header is right and sourced from MULTI_API_KEY env var, all three mandatory resource attributes are present and dynamic (service.version from GIT_SHA, deployment.environment.name from DEPLOY_ENV), Java agent handles http.response.status_code automatically. Should confirm the setup is good and explain what to check at runtime (GIT_SHA must change per deploy, DEPLOY_ENV must differ between environments). Should NOT propose code changes — this is the critical test that the agent respects 'don't rewrite working code'.
